result.adequacy_summary: (a) The binding is genuinely grounded: the dogfood cut #2 ("the skeptic-judge verdict floated free... a found-needle could ship with [FALSIFY]=PASS but no auditable scorecard verdict") maps directly onto §9, and the fix records the verdict into the gated artifact via compliance-block.snippet.md + research.md — real evidence, real closure. (b) The scoping is correct and not over-engineered: structural-only (token present + PASS, deferring substance to the judge) faithfully honors the Cycle-2 lesson that a semantic property must not become a brittle regex gate, so it should NOT be promoted to a full keyword/content gate — and exempting null/HTML/INVALID is the right altitude. (c) BUT the exemption logic opens a real loophole I confirmed live: §9 exempts whenever [NULL]=PASS, and a found-needle VALID output ("needle found" headline, real answer + URL, [FALSIFY]=PASS) that simply sets [NULL]=PASS and omits [SKEPTIC] passes the gate clean (exit 0) — §8 only catches the inverse (NNF headline + NULL=NA), so nothing forces NULL=NA when a needle was actually found. The dodge requires no NNF headline and is therefore invisible to every existing check.

problems.issue: Confirmed loophole: the §9 exemption keys on null_verdict=='PASS', but nothing forces [NULL]=NA when a needle was genuinely found. A found-needle VALID report ("needle found" headline, real Answer with a [retrieved] URL, [FALSIFY]=PASS) that sets [NULL]=PASS and drops the [SKEPTIC] line passes the gate clean (verified: exit 0, compliance_pass: 1). §8's NNF↔NULL consistency check only fires on the *inverse* mismatch (NNF/UNANSWERABLE headline + [NULL]=NA), so a found-needle output never trips it. Net: any report can dodge the new skeptic binding by flipping one token, defeating the entire cycle.
problems.fix: Add a [NULL]=PASS↔found-needle consistency check (the missing half of §8): if final_valid and null_verdict=='PASS' (genuine null) but the artifact carries a substantive found-needle signal — e.g. [FALSIFY]=PASS together with a non-NNF headline and at least one [retrieved] source URL, or a BLUF/Answer line that is not NEEDLE NOT FOUND/UNANSWERABLE — flag it ('[NULL]=PASS declares a null result but the output presents a found needle — set [NULL]=NA and supply [SKEPTIC]'). Closing that contradiction removes the only exit from §9. Add a fixture bad-null-dodge (found-needle headline + [NULL]=PASS + no [SKEPTIC]) that must be caught.

problems.issue: The §9 SKEPTIC binding is unit-covered only on the catch path (bad-skeptic-fail → caught; good-positive → PASS). There is no fixture asserting the *exemption boundary* — that a genuine null result (good-negative, [NULL]=PASS) legitimately ships without [SKEPTIC]. Without it, a future tightening of §9 (e.g. the fix above) could silently start false-positiving honest null reports, and the eval would not notice.
problems.fix: Assert in eval/runner.py (or via the existing good-negative fixture, which already has [NULL]=PASS and no [SKEPTIC]) that good-negative still passes the gate. This pins the exemption as intended behavior and guards it against regressions when §9 is hardened for the loophole.

problems.issue: Minor redundancy / dead branch in §9: the elif tests `'/' not in skeptic['verdict'] and skeptic['verdict'] != 'PASS'`, but an unresolved placeholder ([PASS/REWORK]) is already caught by §3 (verified: 'left unresolved') and an empty/missing token by the `is None` branch. The `'/' not in` guard and the `or 'empty'` in the message are therefore unreachable in practice — harmless but slightly misleading about what §9 actually enforces.
problems.fix: Either drop the `'/' not in skeptic['verdict']` guard (§3 owns placeholders) and simplify to `elif skeptic['verdict'] != 'PASS'`, or add a one-line comment noting §3 pre-screens slash-placeholders so the guard is defensive-only. No behavior change; just clarity.

problems.issue: Pre-existing (NOT §9-specific) parser property: gate verdicts are exact-match against "PASS" on the LAST bracketed token of the line, so a verdict written with extra words inside the bracket — e.g. `[SKEPTIC]: scorecard [PASS — no fatal objections]` — is wrongly flagged as 'did not pass'. RUN-CONFIRMED: this fixture exits 1 with '[SKEPTIC] is PASS — NO FATAL OBJECTIONS'. However, I confirmed FRAME behaves identically (`[FRAME]: x [PASS — clean]` -> '[FRAME] is PASS — CLEAN — not PASS'), so this is a uniform convention inherited from the whole gate, not introduced by the §9 binding, and the canonical template (compliance-block.snippet.md L18) prescribes a bare single token. So strictly the §9 binding is consistent with the rest of the gate; flagging this only for completeness on the false-positive lens.
problems.fix: If you want the gate to tolerate annotated verdicts uniformly, normalize the verdict to the first whitespace-delimited word of the last bracket before comparison (e.g. `verdict.split()[0]` when matching the canonical PASS/FAIL/NA/REWORK vocabulary), applied consistently to ALL PASS_ONLY gates and SKEPTIC — not just §9 — so the convention stays symmetric. Otherwise, leave as-is and rely on the documented single-token template; no change needed for the §9 binding specifically.

problems.issue: Pre-existing (NOT §9-specific) parser property: `gates[gate]` assignment means the LAST line matching `^[GATE]:` wins, so a prose/footnote line that literally begins `[SKEPTIC]: ...` placed AFTER the real fenced compliance block overwrites the recorded PASS verdict and triggers a §9 false fail. RUN-CONFIRMED: a doc with `[SKEPTIC]: the scorecard is archived in our internal vault.` after a valid block exits 1. I confirmed this is general (a trailing `[FINAL]: see the conclusion above` line equally clobbers FINAL -> '[FINAL] is ... must be VALID'), so it affects every gate and predates Cycle 12. The authoring pattern (a line starting exactly `[GATE]:` outside the block) is contrived and low-probability.
problems.fix: Optional hardening shared by all gates: scope gate-line parsing to the fenced ```text compliance block (track fence state while iterating lines) so prose lines starting with `[GATE]:` outside the block cannot overwrite recorded verdicts; or keep the FIRST occurrence per gate. Again apply uniformly, not just to SKEPTIC. Not required to make the §9 binding correct for normally-formatted outputs.

problems.issue: PROBE 1 (KEY) — A confident found-needle ships VALID with NO genuine skeptic pass and NO [SKEPTIC] line at all, by marking [NULL]=PASS. Verified by running the gate on /tmp/claude-0/.../probes/probe1-null-dodge.md: headline '# BLUF — needle found', affirmative Answer, [FALSIFY]=PASS, [NULL]=PASS, [FINAL]=VALID, [SKEPTIC] absent -> output 'OK — compliance gate passed', compliance_pass: 1, exit 0, violations=[]. The §9 binding (compliance_check.py lines 139-140) is guarded by `null_verdict != "PASS"`, so claiming a null result short-circuits the entire skeptic requirement. The gate is asymmetric: §8 (lines 123-133) flags only the inverse case (a NEEDLE-NOT-FOUND/UNANSWERABLE headline with [NULL]=NA), so there is no check for the opposite — an asserted needle in the BLUF/Answer while [NULL]=PASS claims 'no needle was found'. A self-contradictory output (needle asserted + null claimed) is therefore both internally inconsistent AND skips the Cycle-12 gate. This is the exact bypass the cycle was meant to close; IMPROVEMENT.md line 231 lists 'Null results ... are exempt' as design without noting it is forgeable.
problems.fix: Add a symmetric §8-style structural check: when final_valid AND [NULL]=='PASS' (a claimed null result), assert the headline/Answer line does NOT affirmatively declare a needle. Mirror the existing headline scan (only '#'-headings or '**answer' lines, to stay structural and avoid prose false-positives): `affirmative_needle = any((s.startswith('#') or s.lower().startswith('**answer')) and re.search(r'needle found|\bfound\b|answer:', s, re.I) and not re.search(r'needle not found|unanswerable', s, re.I) for s in lines)`; then `if final_valid and null_verdict=='PASS' and affirmative_needle:` append a violation such as '[NULL]=PASS claims a null result, but the answer affirmatively declares a found needle — a found needle is not a null result; set [NULL]=NA and bind a PASS [SKEPTIC] scorecard'. This fixes the internal-contradiction gap AND re-routes the output back through §9 (with [NULL]=NA the `null_verdict != 'PASS'` guard becomes true, so [SKEPTIC]=PASS is required). Add a fixture (e.g. bad-null-dodge) to the frozen eval to lock the regression. Confirmed feasible: this candidate guard returns True on probe1's '# BLUF — needle found' / '**Answer:** ...' lines.

problems.issue: PROBE 2 — [SKEPTIC]=PASS is accepted with NO actual skeptic scorecard in the report body (the seven-failure-mode attack from falsify-skeptic.md is absent; only the bare gate token exists). Verified on /tmp/claude-0/.../probes/probe2-empty-token.md -> PASS, exit 0. The gate checks the token only and never inspects for scorecard content.
problems.fix: No code change strictly required — this IS an acknowledged, documented structural limit: IMPROVEMENT.md Cycle 12 (line 228) explicitly says §9 is 'Structural only (token presence/PASS; the judge owns substance — Cycle 2 lesson)', and the good-positive eval fixture deliberately carries the same bare token. The two-layer design (format gate vs. substance judge, RT5 lines 242-243) intentionally puts substance in the author!=reviewer skeptic-judge, not the regex gate. Optional hardening: require a scorecard marker block (e.g. a fenced 'skeptic-scorecard' snippet naming the 7 modes) co-located with [SKEPTIC]=PASS so the token cannot be asserted without the scorecard pasted in. At minimum, add a one-line note in §9's docstring that an empty/fake [SKEPTIC]=PASS token is a known accepted (judge-owned) limit, so future readers don't mistake it for a hole.

problems.issue: PROBE 3 casing/trailing-text — '[SKEPTIC]: pass' (lowercase, no brackets), '[SKEPTIC]: scorecard verdict [PASS] (full scorecard omitted ...)', and '[SKEPTIC]: scorecard came back [REWORK] but I overrode it to [PASS]' ALL resolve to verdict 'PASS' and ship VALID (verified: probe3a/3b/3c -> exit 0). Parsed verdicts: 3a->'PASS' (via .upper(), line 53), 3b->'PASS' (last bracket), 3c->'PASS' because `verdict = br[-1]` takes the LAST bracket so a self-described overridden-REWORK reads as PASS (tokens=['REWORK','PASS']).
problems.fix: 3a (lowercase) and 3b (trailing prose after a [PASS] token) are correct intended leniency — .upper() normalization and 'last bracket = verdict' are deliberate, with substance owned by the judge, so no fix needed. 3c is a minor parser-leniency edge worth a guard: a [SKEPTIC] (or any PASS_ONLY) line that contains BOTH a REWORK/FAIL token and a PASS token is suspicious (a failed-then-overridden verdict). Optional hardening: if `info['tokens']` contains any of {'REWORK','FAIL'} alongside 'PASS', treat the line as contradictory/unresolved and emit a violation ('[SKEPTIC] line carries conflicting verdict tokens (REWORK and PASS) — record a single resolved verdict'). Low priority; the author!=reviewer judge layer is the real backstop.

problems.issue: §9 exempts a found-needle output from the [SKEPTIC] requirement whenever null_verdict == "PASS" (the condition `null_verdict != "PASS"`). Because nothing ties [NULL]=PASS to an actual NEEDLE-NOT-FOUND headline (§8 only checks the NA<->NNF direction, never PASS<->found-needle), a genuine found-needle VALID output can DROP the [SKEPTIC] line entirely and simply flip [NULL] from NA to PASS to pass the whole gate with zero violations. Verified empirically: good-positive with the [SKEPTIC] line removed and [NULL] changed NA->PASS yields zero violations / exit 0, even though the headline still says "needle found" and gives a concrete answer. This pre-dates Cycle 12 (NULL=PASS on a found needle was already unguarded), but Cycle 12's binding newly makes [NULL]=PASS a one-switch skeptic-bypass, so the new gate is only as strong as the (currently unchecked) NULL label. This does NOT affect any frozen-fixture result, so it is a hardening gap, not a regression.
problems.fix: Add a guard so [NULL]=PASS is only honored as a skeptic-exemption when the output actually declares a null result. Reuse the existing headline_nnf signal: in §9 treat the output as a found-needle (skeptic-required) unless headline_nnf is true, e.g. compute `is_null_result = (null_verdict == "PASS" and headline_nnf)` and gate §9 on `not is_null_result` instead of `null_verdict != "PASS"`. Optionally also add a §8-style check that flags [NULL]=PASS with a non-NNF headline as self-contradictory. Add an adversarial fixture (found-needle headline + [NULL]=PASS + no [SKEPTIC], expected exit 1) to freeze the fix.

reports.summary: (a) The binding is genuinely grounded: the dogfood cut #2 ("the skeptic-judge verdict floated free... a found-needle could ship with [FALSIFY]=PASS but no auditable scorecard verdict") maps directly onto §9, and the fix records the verdict into the gated artifact via compliance-block.snippet.md + research.md — real evidence, real closure. (b) The scoping is correct and not over-engineered: structural-only (token present + PASS, deferring substance to the judge) faithfully honors the Cycle-2 lesson that a semantic property must not become a brittle regex gate, so it should NOT be promoted to a full keyword/content gate — and exempting null/HTML/INVALID is the right altitude. (c) BUT the exemption logic opens a real loophole I confirmed live: §9 exempts whenever [NULL]=PASS, and a found-needle VALID output ("needle found" headline, real answer + URL, [FALSIFY]=PASS) that simply sets [NULL]=PASS and omits [SKEPTIC] passes the gate clean (exit 0) — §8 only catches the inverse (NNF headline + NULL=NA), so nothing forces NULL=NA when a needle was actually found. The dodge requires no NNF headline and is therefore invisible to every existing check.

Red-teamed the Cycle 12 [SKEPTIC] gate binding (§9, lines 135-145 of scripts/compliance_check.py) plus its main() wiring by RUNNING the script on crafted markdown/HTML. All five required probes pass correctly: (1) honest NEEDLE-NOT-FOUND with [NULL]=PASS and NO [SKEPTIC] line PASSES (exit 0) — §9 is exempted by the `null_verdict != "PASS"` guard on line 140; (2) found-needle with [SKEPTIC]=PASS PASSES; (3) [FINAL]=INVALID with no [SKEPTIC] is flagged ONLY by §4's INVALID rule, NOT by §9 — `final_valid` is False so §9 never runs; (4) the HTML path routes to analyze_html() (main() line 283-284) so §9 never runs and the doc passes; (5) the official eval (eval/runner.py) still reports detection 1.00 and false_positive_rate 0.00 — good-negative, good-positive, and good-report-html all PASS. I further probed 12 legitimate edge shapes (SKEPTIC verdict as bracketed [PASS], bare-word `PASS`, lowercase `[pass]`, whitespace-padded `[ PASS ]`, trailing prose, FINAL with trailing words, null result carrying SKEPTIC=PASS or SKEPTIC=NA, prose mentions of [SKEPTIC]): every legitimately-formatted output PASSES. The §9 binding uses the same exact-match `== "PASS"` verdict rule and last-bracket parsing convention as every other PASS_ONLY gate (FRAME, ABDUCT, ...), and the canonical template (templates/compliance-block.snippet.md line 18) mandates a single trailing `[PASS/REWORK]` token, so §9 introduces NO new false-positive surface. The two false positives I could induce — extra words inside the verdict bracket (e.g. `[PASS — no fatal objections]`) and a prose line starting `[SKEPTIC]:` placed AFTER the fenced block clobbering the real verdict — are uniform parser properties shared by ALL gates (I confirmed FRAME and FINAL behave identically), predate Cycle 12, and represent deviations from the documented single-token contract rather than §9-specific binding defects. Conclusion: the §9 [SKEPTIC] binding does not wrongly FAIL a legitimately-formatted output.

RAN /home/user/needle-in-a-haystack/scripts/compliance_check.py on 6 crafted markdown files plus the good-positive / bad-skeptic-fail controls. Controls behaved: good-positive -> PASS (exit 0); bad-skeptic-fail ([SKEPTIC]=REWORK) -> caught (exit 1). THE KEY PROBE confirms a real, undocumented bypass: a confident found-needle (headline "# BLUF — needle found", "**Answer:** ... defaults to 2000") that marks [NULL]=PASS and OMITS the [SKEPTIC] line entirely ships VALID with ZERO violations (exit 0). The §9 guard is `final_valid AND falsify_pass AND null_verdict != "PASS"` (lines 139-140), so asserting [NULL]=PASS (claiming a null result) makes the condition false and the skeptic requirement is never evaluated — no [SKEPTIC] needed. Nothing else catches it: §8 (lines 123-133) only flags the INVERSE direction (a "needle not found / unanswerable" headline with [NULL]=NA); there is NO check for "needle asserted in BLUF/Answer but [NULL]=PASS". The gate is asymmetric and the central skeptic binding is trivially dodged by lying on one token. Probe 2 ([SKEPTIC]=PASS token present, body has no actual seven-mode scorecard) PASSES — but this is an ACKNOWLEDGED, documented structural limit: IMPROVEMENT.md Cycle 12 line 228 says "Structural only (token presence/PASS; the judge owns substance)", and the eval's own good-positive fixture carries the same bare token, so token-only checking is intended design, not a defect. Probe 3 casing/trailing-text tricks all PASS but that is mostly by-design normalization, not a bypass: ".upper()" (line 53) makes "[SKEPTIC]: pass" -> PASS; "verdict = last bracket" (br[-1]) makes "scorecard verdict [PASS] (omitted for brevity)" -> PASS; and "came back [REWORK] but I overrode it to [PASS]" also -> PASS because the LAST bracket wins (tokens=['REWORK','PASS']) — the first two are intentional leniency (substance owned by the judge), the third is a minor parser-leniency edge worth a guard. Net: one high-severity bypass (Probe 1 NULL dodge), one acknowledged/documented limit (Probe 2), one minor parser note (Probe 3c).

Ran every required check against scripts/compliance_check.py at HEAD (Cycle 12, commit 3ce3d5e). ALL REGRESSION CHECKS PASS, no regression found. eval/runner.py: 12/12 detection + 0/3 FP, eval_pass:1, exit 0. tests/test_check_links.py: green, exit 0 (run standalone the way CI runs it — `python tests/test_check_links.py`; note pytest is NOT installed in this env and the file is a plain script, not a pytest suite, so `python -m pytest` fails on missing-module only, not on test content). Default (no --check-links) plain-text output and exit codes for all 13 markdown fixtures are unchanged and correct (good=0, all bad=1). good-positive (/home/user/needle-in-a-haystack/eval/fixtures/good-positive/report.md) now carries [SKEPTIC]: ... [PASS], parses all 13 gates, zero violations, exit 0. bad-skeptic-fail (/home/user/needle-in-a-haystack/eval/fixtures/bad-skeptic-fail/report.md) fails via §9 ALONE — exactly one violation ("[SKEPTIC] is REWORK ..."), exit 1. Consistency: the [SKEPTIC] line is token-identical ([PASS/REWORK]) and identically placed (after [NULL], before [FINAL]) across templates/compliance-block.snippet.md:18, references/research.md:150, and the fixtures. §9 (scripts/compliance_check.py:135-146) is purely additive — appended after §8, before the de-dup return; the GATE_LINE/BRACKET parser and the gates-dict build are untouched, so adding [SKEPTIC] did NOT perturb parsing of the other 12 gates (confirmed: good-positive's other gates all still parse PASS with zero violations). SKEPTIC is correctly excluded from REQUIRED_GATES and PASS_ONLY, so the genuine-null good-negative fixture (no [SKEPTIC] line, [NULL]=PASS) is exempt and still passes. Edge cases fail closed: dropped line -> "carries no [SKEPTIC]" violation; empty/FAIL/REWORK -> "not PASS" violation; unfilled [PASS/REWORK] placeholder -> caught by §3 as unresolved. All three CI steps (py_compile, runner, link test) reproduce green. One non-regression integration-hardening observation noted in problems[].
